title: What If Every Mosquito Went Extinct?

scenes.text: What if every mosquito on Earth went extinct tomorrow? Scientists have actually studied this.
There are about three and a half thousand species. Only a few hundred bite humans.
Malaria alone kills around six hundred thousand people a year. Those deaths would stop.
In the Arctic, mosquito swarms feed migrating birds and even steer caribou herds. Those would shift.
Their larvae feed fish and frogs. But almost every one of those has other food.
Scientists' verdict in the journal Nature: nature would barely notice, and humans would be far better off.
